concerns.text: Tasks T015, T016b, and T016c implement a hard 'Negative Finding' abort path when no single dataset is found. This silently weakens FR-001 and SC-001, which explicitly mandate identifying separate 'Simulated-Only' and 'Real-Only' datasets for meta-analysis as a valid success state. The tasks treat a spec-defined success criterion as a failure state.

Task T014 categorizes datasets into 'Sim-Only' and 'Real-Only' but the subsequent logic (T015) discards these as 'Negative Findings' rather than fulfilling FR-001's requirement to 'identify separate datasets... to enable meta-analysis'. The deliverable of T014 is effectively nullified by T015, violating the spec's continuity requirement.

Task T052 implements the sensitivity sweep by re-running the entire preprocessing pipeline (T020) for each threshold. This violates the semantic intent of FR-006, which requires sweeping the 'artifact-rejection voltage threshold' (a post-epoching QC parameter). Re-running the full pipeline (filtering, ICA, epoching) is a semantic relaxation of the efficiency and methodological constraints implied by the spec, conflating preprocessing with rejection logic.

Task T017 implements error handling for missing anxiety measures by logging and triggering an abort (T015). This violates the Spec's 'Assumptions' section which mandates a 'manual review protocol' to expand keywords or search alternative repos (Zenodo, Figshare) before escalating to human intervention or aborting. The task skips the required fallback protocol.

Task T044 defines 'stability' strictly as p < 0.05 across all thresholds OR p > 0.05 across all thresholds. This weakens SC-003, which requires 'conclusions' to remain stable. A conclusion can be stable (e.g., consistent effect direction and magnitude) even if p-values fluctuate near the 0.05 threshold. The task's binary logic risks false negatives in stability checks, failing to satisfy the semantic requirement of SC-003.
